title: Latent non-Gaussian models with ngvb
text: latent Gaussian model (LGM), workhorse R-INLA, places Gaussian prior latent field: random walk, autoregression, spatial effect, set random effects. prior convenient rigid, assumes Gaussianity everywhere. Real data often break assumption just places, sudden jump time series, one outlying subject, sharp boundary regions, local hotspot space. Gaussian model compromise. either -smooths interesting feature inflates variance everywhere accommodate . ngvb relaxes single assumption. keeps everything already , INLA model code, replaces Gaussian driving noise heavier-tailed one. result adds flexibility data ask falls back Gaussian model everywhere else. Two functions work, take ordinary inla fit run control.compute = list(config = TRUE): ng.check(fit) asks whether relax Gaussian assumption, . ngvb(fit) fits non-Gaussian extension.

Conditional 𝐕\mathbf V field still Gaussian, precision 𝐐(𝛉,𝐕)=𝐃(𝛉)⊤diag(1/𝐕)𝐃(𝛉).\mathbf Q(\boldsymbol\theta,\mathbf V)=\mathbf D(\boldsymbol\theta)^\top\,    \mathrm{diag}(1/\mathbf V)\,\mathbf D(\boldsymbol\theta).ngvb fits model short variational-Bayes loop repeatedly calls INLA 𝐕\mathbf V fixed updates 𝐕\mathbf V η\eta. prior η\eta exponential (penalised-complexity prior rate alpha.eta, default 22) shrinks toward Gaussian model, non-Gaussianity earn place. code: ggplot(jumpts, aes(x, y)) +   geom_line(colour = "grey70") +   geom_point(colour = "grey30", size = 1.3) +   labs(title = "jumpts", x = "time", y = "y") +   theme_minimal(base_size = 12) LGM <- inla(y ~ -1 + f(x, model = "rw1"), data = jumpts,             control.compute = list(config = TRUE)) check <- ng.check(LGM, compute.fixed = FALSE) LnGM <- ngvb(LGM) #> Components: x [rw1] #> ngvb: converged after 24 iteration(s);  E[eta] = 3.742 plot(LnGM) samples <- ngvb_sample(LnGM, n.samples = 30) bayes.factor(samples)               # LnGM vs. LGM marginal-likelihood ratio #> Bayes factor (non-Gaussian vs Gaussian): 9.95e+23 #>   log10 BF = 24.00  (decisive) #>   weight ESS = 2.2 of 30 draws summary(samples)                    # importance-weighted summaries, V integrated out #> Latent non-Gaussian model, V integrated out over 30 draws #> Bayes factor vs Gaussian model: 9.95e+23 (log10 = 24.00), weight ESS 2.2 #>  #> Fixed effects: #>   (none) #>  #> Hyperparameters: #>                                              mean         sd #> Precision for the Gaussian observations 3583.4354 13654.6354 #> Theta1 for x                               2.1163     0.4493 #>  #> Random effects: #>   $x (100 nodes) #>   ID    mean     sd #> 1  1 -0.8755 0.1419 #> 2  2 -0.6634 0.1094 #> 3  3 -0.7070 0.0956 #> 4  4 -0.6998 0.0999 #> 5  5 -0.8781 0.1213 #> 6  6 -0.7240 0.1306 #>   ... 94 more row(s); use what = "random" to print in full

title: Latent non-Gaussian models with ngvb
text: weatherdata, bundled package, holds pressure readings across Pacific Northwest. Build mesh first plot stations :  model pressure continuous Matern field SPDE approach, standard tool point-referenced spatial data. field solves stochastic PDE whose finite-element form gives operator 𝐃=κ2𝐂+𝐆\mathbf D=\kappa^2\mathbf C+\mathbf G, 𝐂\mathbf C 𝐆\mathbf G mass stiffness matrices mesh. Gaussian Matern smooths whole surface uniformly, non-Gaussian version lets locations depart sharply. ngvb reads 𝐃\mathbf D straight fitted spde object, pass nothing extra.  ng.check()’s diagnostic di(y)d_i(y) one instance general result (Theorem 2 Cabral, Bolin & Rue, JRSS-B 2025): sensitivity posterior summary relaxing Gaussianity covariance, computable entirely Gaussian fit, without ever running ngvb(). Two instances built : sensitivity covariate’s coefficient (chk$sens.fixed, one column per fixed effect) sensitivity latent field’s posterior mean every node (chk$sens.random$s, available ng.check() called compute.random = TRUE ). ever fitting non-Gaussian model, can already map predictions expected move :  map computed entirely Gaussian fit ; ngvb() run yet. can tell regions spatial predictions change , also direction. Blue means posterior mean latent field take larger values fit non-Gaussian model.  mixing variables live mesh nodes, can map back space. plot ratio Vi/hiV_i/h_i, one field Gaussian larger departs uniform Matern (SPDE weights hih_i mesh mass, Vi/hiV_i/h_i rather ViV_i quantity look ):  ngvb_sample() also pools latent field summary(samples, = "random"), can now compare sensitivity preview actual /change posterior mean:  two maps pick location. sensitivity preview correlates actual change magnitude, among handful nodes flags sensitive direction agrees :
code: w    <- read.csv(system.file("extdata", "weatherdata.csv", package = "ngvb")) mesh <- inla.mesh.2d(loc = w[, c("lon", "lat")], max.edge = c(1.5, 2.5),                      cutoff = 0.3, max.n.strict = 400) geo.plot(w[, c("lon", "lat", "press")], mesh = mesh, title = "pressure",          palette = "RdBu") spde <- inla.spde2.pcmatern(mesh, alpha = 2,                             prior.range = c(1, 0.5),    # P(range < 1) = 0.5                             prior.sigma = c(10, 0.1))   # P(sigma > 1) = 0.01 A    <- inla.spde.make.A(mesh, loc = as.matrix(w[, c("lon", "lat")])) stk  <- inla.stack(tag = "est", data = list(y = w$press), A = list(A),                    effects = list(s = 1:spde$n.spde))  LGM <- inla(y ~ -1 + f(s, model = spde), data = inla.stack.data(stk),             control.predictor = list(A = inla.stack.A(stk)),             control.compute = list(config = TRUE)) chk <- ng.check(LGM, compute.random = TRUE) nodes.sens <- data.frame(lon = mesh$loc[, 1], lat = mesh$loc[, 2], sens = chk$sens.random$s) geo.plot(nodes.sens, mesh = mesh, title = "sensitivity of posterior mean", palette = "RdBu") LnGM <- ngvb(LGM) #> Components: s [spde] #> ngvb: reached the iteration limit after 30 iteration(s);  E[eta] = 0.096 plot(LnGM) nodes <- data.frame(lon = mesh$loc[, 1], lat = mesh$loc[, 2],                     Vh = LnGM$V$s / LnGM$h$s) geo.plot(nodes, mesh = mesh, title = "V/h") samples <- ngvb_sample(LnGM, n.samples = 30, seed = 1) bayes.factor(samples) #> Bayes factor (non-Gaussian vs Gaussian): 47.1 #>   log10 BF = 1.67  (strong) #>   weight ESS = 12.9 of 30 draws post    <- summary(samples, verbose = FALSE)  diff <- post$random$s$mean - LGM$summary.random$s$mean nodes.diff <- data.frame(lon = mesh$loc[, 1], lat = mesh$loc[, 2], diff = diff) geo.plot(nodes.diff, mesh = mesh, title = "LnGM - LGM (posterior mean)", palette = "RdBu") cat(sprintf("correlation(sensitivity, actual change) = %.2f\n",             cor(chk$sens.random$s, diff))) #> correlation(sensitivity, actual change) = 0.78 top10 <- order(-abs(chk$sens.random$s))[1:20] cat(sprintf("sign agreement among the 20 most sensitive nodes: %.0f%%\n",             100 * mean(sign(chk$sens.random$s[top10]) == sign(diff[top10])))) #> sign agreement among the 20 most sensitive nodes: 100%

title: Latent non-Gaussian models with ngvb
text: Orthodont records growth measurement 27 children four ages, together sex indicator time coded two ways. quick look raw data frame:  Two kinds child--child variation matter . child starts different height, variation intercept, child grows slightly different rate, variation slope. give every child intercept slope, two iid random effects: valueij=β0+βcovariates+asubject(ij)⏟random intercept+bsubject(ij)timeij⏟random slope+εij,\text{value}_{ij} = \beta_0 + \beta\,\text{covariates}    + \underbrace{a_{\text{subject}(ij)}}_{\text{random intercept}}    + \underbrace{b_{\text{subject}(ij)}\,\text{time}_{ij}}_{\text{random slope}}    + \varepsilon_{ij}, ak∼N(0,1/τa)a_k \sim N(0, 1/\tau_a) bk∼N(0,1/τb)b_k \sim N(0, 1/\tau_b) across children. make random effects non-Gaussian? Gaussian random effect treats children exchangeable draws one normal distribution. child two genuine outliers, unusually high baseline example, Gaussian either shrinks toward mean hides outlier, widens distribution everyone accommodate . non-Gaussian random effect keeps tight distribution typical children lets outliers stand . ng.check() reports one diagnostic per component:  see substancial evidence non-Gaussianity found (small pp) random effects.  fitting latent non-Gaussian model see intercept carries non-Gaussianity slope. couple children outlying baselines, growth rates close Gaussian.
code: Orthodont$age <- c(8, 10, 12, 14)[Orthodont$time + 1]  ggplot(Orthodont, aes(x = age, y = value)) +   geom_line(color = "#007fff") +   geom_point(shape = 1, color = "#007fff") +   scale_x_continuous(breaks = c(9, 11, 13)) +    facet_wrap(~ ifelse(Female == 1, paste0("F", subject), paste0("M", subject)), ncol = 11) +   theme_bw() +   theme(panel.spacing = unit(0, "lines"),         strip.background = element_rect(fill = "#ffe5cc")) formula <- value ~ 1 + Female + time + tF +   f(subject,  model = "iid") +      # random intercept, one per child   f(subject2, time, model = "iid")  # random slope, one per child  LGM <- inla(formula, data = Orthodont, control.compute = list(config = TRUE)) ng.check(LGM, compute.fixed = FALSE) LnGM <- ngvb(LGM) #> Components: subject [iid], subject2 [iid] #> ngvb: reached the iteration limit after 30 iteration(s);  E[eta] = 0.130, 0.203 plot(LnGM) bayes.factor(LnGM, n.samples = 30, seed = 1) #> Bayes factor (non-Gaussian vs Gaussian): 7.88e+05 #>   log10 BF = 5.90  (decisive) #>   weight ESS = 3.1 of 30 draws

text: Residential burglary rates 49 counties Columbus, Ohio, come spData package. Plot response map first:  intrinsic conditional autoregression (besag model) assumes neighbouring counties similar, Gaussian differences across edges adjacency graph, xi−xj∼N(0,1/τ)edge (,j).x_i - x_j \sim N(0,\,1/\tau)\quad\text{edge }(,j). non-Gaussian version allows sharp boundaries otherwise smooth regions. Build adjacency fit Gaussian model:  118 edges graph show similarly small discrepancy Gaussian reference. field essentially Gaussian, previous checking procedure (ng.check) latent non-Gaussian fitting (ngvb) show .
code: library(sf); library(spdep) map  <- st_read(system.file("shapes/columbus.gpkg", package = "spData"), quiet = TRUE) areal.plot(map, map$CRIME, title = "crime") d    <- st_drop_geometry(map[, c("CRIME", "HOVAL", "INC")]) d$s  <- seq_len(nrow(d)) nb   <- poly2nb(map) Wadj <- Matrix::sparseMatrix(i = rep(seq_along(nb), lengths(nb)), j = unlist(nb), x = 1)  LGM <- inla(CRIME ~ 1 + HOVAL + INC +               f(s, model = "besag", graph = Wadj, scale.model = TRUE,                 hyper = list(prec = list(prior = "loggamma", param = c(0.5, 0.01)))),             data = d, control.compute = list(config = TRUE)) LGM$summary.hyperpar #>                                               mean           sd  0.025quant #> Precision for the Gaussian observations  0.0080316  0.001644847 0.005242204 #> Precision for s                         57.1638799 89.632926477 1.289090539 #>                                             0.5quant   0.975quant        mode #> Precision for the Gaussian observations  0.007880677   0.01168902 0.007604842 #> Precision for s                         27.942104820 284.83005906 2.349096011 ng.check(LGM, compute.fixed = FALSE)   # areal model auto-detected LnGM <- ngvb(LGM) #> Components: s [car] #> ngvb: reached the iteration limit after 30 iteration(s);  E[eta] = 0.073 plot(LnGM) bayes.factor(LnGM, n.samples = 30, seed = 1) #> Bayes factor (non-Gaussian vs Gaussian): 1.04 #>   log10 BF = 0.02  (weak/none) #>   weight ESS = 25.6 of 30 draws

Unlike intrinsic besag effect, SAR mixing variables live counties , can map directly. full definition, argument explained just . arguments : D = function(theta) builds dependency matrix 𝐃(𝛉)\mathbf D(\boldsymbol\theta) sparse Matrix. rows driving-noise terms columns latent nodes. theta[1] log precision theta[2] internal (unconstrained) version ρ\rho, mapped (0,1)(0,1) logistic function. INLA works internal scale, transform appears inside D. h constant vector E[Vi]=hiE[V_i]=h_i, V=hV=h recovers Gaussian model. discrete areal model one innovation per node, h vector ones. ntheta number hyperparameters INLA estimates, two. logprior = function(theta) log prior density hyperparameters, written internal scale including change--variables Jacobian. piece INLA adds log-posterior 𝛉\boldsymbol\theta. example N(0,3)N(0,3) prior log precision, uniform prior ρ∈(0,1)\rho\(0,1); logistic transform uniform density contributes Jacobian term log⁡ρ+log⁡(1−ρ)\log\rho + \log(1-\rho). omit logprior, independent N(0,3)N(0,3) internal hyperparameter used. lognc = function(theta, Vinv) optional recommended 𝐃\mathbf D can get close singular, ρ\rho approaches one. returns log normalizing constant conditional Gaussian density, 12log⁡|𝐐(𝛉,𝐕)|−n2log⁡(2π)\tfrac12\log|\mathbf Q(\boldsymbol\theta,\mathbf V)| - \tfrac{n}{2}\log(2\pi), receives Vinv =1/𝐕=1/\mathbf V 𝐕\mathbf V-dependent part determinant included. SAR log-determinant closed form Nlog⁡τ+2∑ilog⁡(1−ρλi)+∑ilog⁡(1/Vi)N\log\tau + 2\sum_i\log(1-\rho\lambda_i) + \sum_i\log(1/V_i), using eigenvalues λi\lambda_i 𝐖\mathbf W, fast stable near boundary. lognc omitted, engine computes determinant generically, fine well-conditioned operators. couple practical notes. D, logprior, lognc evaluated separate R process base packages attached, non-base function must namespace-qualified, code writes Matrix::Diagonal stats::dnorm, uses exp(t)/(1+exp(t)) rather plogis. data functions reference, W eigenv, captured automatically. operator defined, fit Gaussian SAR engine extend :  SAR weights live counties, can put straight back map. Low values yellow high values red, reddest counties model added flexibility, meaning largest local departures smooth spatial field:  whole custom interface. Give ngvb_custom() function D(theta) vector h, optionally prior normalizing constant, Gaussian model whose precision factors 𝐃⊤diag(1/𝐡)𝐃\mathbf D^\top\mathrm{diag}(1/\mathbf h)\mathbf D becomes latent non-Gaussian one.
code: W      <- Matrix::Diagonal(x = 1 / rowSums(Wadj)) %*% Wadj    # row-standardise N      <- nrow(W) eigenv <- Re(eigen(as.matrix(W), only.values = TRUE)$values)  op_sar <- ngvb_custom(   D = function(theta) {     rho <- exp(theta[2]) / (1 + exp(theta[2]))     sqrt(exp(theta[1])) * (Matrix::Diagonal(N) - rho * W)   },   h        = rep(1, N),   ntheta   = 2,   logprior = function(theta) {     rho <- exp(theta[2]) / (1 + exp(theta[2]))     stats::dnorm(theta[1], 0, 3, log = TRUE) + log(rho) + log(1 - rho)   },   lognc = function(theta, Vinv) {     rho <- exp(theta[2]) / (1 + exp(theta[2]))     0.5 * N * theta[1] + sum(log(1 - rho * eigenv)) +       0.5 * sum(log(Vinv)) - 0.5 * N * log(2 * pi)   }) LGM  <- inla(CRIME ~ 1 + HOVAL + INC + f(s, model = ngvb_rgeneric(op_sar)),              data = d, control.compute = list(config = TRUE)) LnGM <- ngvb(LGM, components = list(s = op_sar), verbose = FALSE) plot(LnGM) areal.plot(map, LnGM$V$s, title = "V") bayes.factor(LnGM, n.samples = 30, seed = 1) #> Bayes factor (non-Gaussian vs Gaussian): 9.59 #>   log10 BF = 0.98  (substantial) #>   weight ESS = 15.4 of 30 draws

AR(1) field, example: theta[1] added precision hyperparameter; theta[2] passed straight ngme2’s update_K, applies internal transform .
code: ngme_ar1 <- ngme2::ar1(1:N)  op_ar1_ngme2 <- ngvb_custom(   D = function(theta) sqrt(exp(theta[1])) * ngme_ar1$update_K(theta[2]),   h        = ngme_ar1$h,   ntheta   = 2,   logprior = function(theta) {     stats::dnorm(theta[1], 0, 3, log = TRUE) +   # precision: your choice     stats::dnorm(theta[2], 0, 1, log = TRUE)     # matches ngme2's own prior_normal(0, 1) on theta_K   })

what: Latent non-Gaussian models with R-INLA and variational Bayes
title: Latent non-Gaussian models with R-INLA and variational Bayes
text: ngvb (non-Gaussian variational Bayes) takes ordinary R-INLA latent Gaussian model (LGM), checks whether latent Gaussian assumption adequate, extends latent non-Gaussian model (LnGM), one line.
code: LGM <- inla(y ~ f(s, model = "rw1"), data = d, control.compute = list(config = TRUE))  ng.check(LGM)       # is the latent Gaussian assumption adequate, and where not? LnGM <- ngvb(LGM)   # fit the non-Gaussian extension  samples <- ngvb_sample(LnGM, n.samples = 30) # sample non-gaussian V from the variational posterior + fit R-INLA models bayes.factor(samples)               # how much better the LnGM is, with V integrated out? summary(samples)                    # summary of random effects + fixed effects + hyperparameters of the LnGM

text: fit `inla` object fitted `control.compute = list(config = TRUE)`. selection Optional named list components check (default: random). components Optional operator overrides (e.g. SPDE), [ngvb()]. compute.fixed `TRUE`, also return sensitivity fixed effect component's non-Gaussianity parameter. compute.random `TRUE`, also return, checked component, sensitivity ** posterior mean every node non-Gaussianity – .e. much node's fitted value move [ngvb()], estimated base (Gaussian) fit alone, without actually fitting non-Gaussian model. Bayes-factor-sensitivity theory used `sens.fixed` (Theorem 2 Cabral, Bolin & Rue, JRSS-B 2025), applied component's field instead fixed effect: reuses cross-covariance already computed `d`, costs one extra matrix multiply per hyperparameter configuration, refit. what: Define a custom latent non-Gaussian model from a precision
title: Define a custom latent non-Gaussian model from a precision
text: Supply dependency matrix `D(theta)` (function hyperparameters INLA fits, internal/unconstrained scale) constant vector `h`. field conditional precision `Q(V) = D(theta)^T diag(1/V) D(theta)`, `V = h` recovers Gaussian model. turns ** Gaussian model whose precision factors `Q = D^T diag(1/h) D` latent non-Gaussian one, without hand-writing rgeneric.

title: Define a custom latent non-Gaussian model from a precision
code: ngvb_custom(   D,   h = 1,   ntheta,   theta.initial = rep(0, ntheta),   logprior = function(theta) sum(stats::dnorm(theta, 0, 3, log = TRUE)),   rankdef = 0L,   graph = NULL,   lognc = NULL )

title: Define a custom latent non-Gaussian model from a precision
text: D `function(theta)` returning sparse dependency matrix `D(theta)`, dimension `m x n` (`m` driving-noise terms, `n` latent nodes). h constant vector length `m` (`E[V] = h`; `1` discrete models). scalar recycled. ntheta number hyperparameters. theta.initial initial hyperparameters (internal scale). logprior `function(theta)` log prior internal scale (including Jacobians). Default: independent `N(0, 3)`. rankdef rank deficiency `D^T D` (0 = proper; positive intrinsic models `m < n` difference operators). graph optional sparsity pattern `D^T D` (union `theta`); computed `D(theta.initial)` omitted. lognc optional analytic normalizing constant `function(theta, Vinv)` returning `0.5 log|Q| - 0.5 n log(2 pi)`. Supply generic determinant numerically unstable (e.g. `D` near-singular, SAR/CAR).

title: Define a custom latent non-Gaussian model from a precision
text: operator descriptor use [ngvb()] / [ng.check()] via   `components`, build Gaussian fit via [ngvb_rgeneric()].

title: Define a custom latent non-Gaussian model from a precision
text: Typical workflow: build `op`, fit Gaussian LGM `f(idx, model = ngvb_rgeneric(op))`, call `ng.check(fit, components = ...)` `ngvb(fit, components = ...)`.

title: Define a custom latent non-Gaussian model from a precision
text: `D`, `logprior` `lognc` evaluated separate R process   base packages attached. Data reference (matrices, vectors)   captured automatically, *non-base function* must namespace-qualified   (e.g. `Matrix::Diagonal`, `stats::dnorm`) written base R. instance   use `exp(t)/(1 + exp(t))` rather `plogis(t)`.

title: Define a custom latent non-Gaussian model from a precision
code: # First differences by hand (an RW1), showing the custom interface: n  <- 8 D0 <- Matrix::bandSparse(n - 1, n, c(0, 1), list(rep(-1, n - 1), rep(1, n - 1))) op <- ngvb_custom(D = function(theta) sqrt(exp(theta[1])) * D0,                   h = 1, ntheta = 1, rankdef = 1) dim(op$Dfunc(0)) #> [1] 7 8

text: object `ngvb.samples` object. One `""` (default), `"fixed"`, `"hyperpar"`, `"random"` – INLA summary table(s) pool. `"random"` pools `summary.random` every component (latent field : one table per component, keyed node `ID`, e.g. mesh node time index). `""` shows returns three, silently skipping apply model (e.g. `"fixed"` fixed-effect-free model); random-effect tables printed head (rows still returned). Run `args(summary.ngvb.samples)` `?summary.ngvb.samples` see list . verbose `TRUE` (default), print report side effect (`ng.check()` plot).
